text.p: Israeli inflation-linked bonds closed sharply higher on Sunday for the third consecutive session as investors predicted 1997 inflation may rise steeply, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.03 pct to 103.12
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.15 pct at 102.53
Volume was moderate at 179 million shekels.
"This is really crazy. Everybody wants to buy short-CPI-linked bonds and there are no sellers," said one trader.

"Short-inflation-linked bonds continue to surge as the market is afraid that inflation might accelerate in the next quarter. Investors who did not get short bonds bought medium-term and long bonds," said Danny Shamir at Israel Discount Bank.
Traders noted that Bank Hapoalim raised its CPI forecast for February to 1.2 percent from less than one percent.
"The Bank of Israel might need to issue more long-CPI-linked bonds to cover the soaring budget deficit and the pressure on short bonds rises," Shamir added.
"Unlinked bonds rose mildly while long unlinked bonds closed lower but investors focused on linked bonds now," said Ari Eidelheit at Zeller Eblgon Securities.
Traders said dollar-linked bonds continued their rise after the dollar climbed sharply against the shekel on Thursday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
